svg.title: An idempotent retry can undo an intervening operation
svg.desc: Time proceeds downward along three timelines: client 1, database and client 2. Client 1 sends f, add like. The database applies it but its acknowledgement is lost, shown with a black cross before it reaches client 1. Client 2 sees the updated set of likes L and sends g, unlike, removing the same userID. The database applies g and acknowledges client 2. Client 1 retries f, which restores that like, and receives an acknowledgement. Both clients act on the same userID, such as two devices of the same user. Definitions: f(L) is L union {userID}; g(L) is L minus {userID}. Although f(f(L)) equals f(L), f(g(f(L))) differs from g(f(L)). The example assumes the database applies the retried operation again rather than deduplicating it by a request identifier.
svg.metadata: Redrawn from the user-supplied Martin Kleppmann slide Adding and then removing again. LaTeX/TikZ, Latin Modern fonts, monochrome square boxes and matching arrowheads. All text is preserved as vector outlines.
